cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: ConfigMap and Secret both inject configuration into a Pod as environment variables or mounted files, without hard-coding values into the image. ConfigMap is for non-sensitive values like feature flags, paths and URLs; Secret is for sensitive values like passwords and API keys.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: A Secret's data field is only Base64-encoded, not encrypted, so anyone with API or etcd access can decode it. Real protection comes from RBAC and encryption at rest that the cluster operator configures. stringData lets you write a Secret as plain text and Kubernetes encodes it.

questions.q: Is a value in a Secret encrypted by default?
questions.a: No. It is only Base64-encoded, which is reversible encoding, not encryption.
RBAC limiting who can read them and encryption at rest configured by the cluster operator.

questions.q: How can a Pod consume ConfigMaps and Secrets?
questions.a: As environment variables or as mounted files.
